cues.en: So as I mentioned, there are two methods of dynamic programming for solving problems.
Top down with memoization and bottom up with tabulation.
So let's look at first the first one which is top down with memoization.
So this solves the problem by breaking into the subproblems recursively and storing their results.
So here we divide the problem into subproblems and then solve these subproblems and combine together.
Now in this approach we solve the bigger problem by recursively finding the solution to the smaller
subproblems.
Whenever we solve the subproblem, we save its result so we don't end up solving it repeatedly if it
is called multiple times.
Instead, we just return the saved result.
So the technique of storing the results of already solved subproblems is called memoization.
Basically, what we are doing over here is we are dividing the problem into subproblems.
Then solve the subproblems.
And the solutions to these subproblems are stored to be used for future cases.
When we face the same subproblem here, the main idea is to start from the top, which is the main problem.
Then continue to the down by dividing the main problem into the subproblems.
Now, to make this clear, let's look at one more time the Fibonacci example that we explained in Divide
and conquer section.
So we know that in a Fibonacci series, the current number is obtained by adding the previous two numbers
and find the first two numbers that are zero and one.
So we are using this calculation based on this.
If we calculate it, we are getting the Fibonacci series like this.
Now if you look at this equation, we can easily see that we have two recursive calls over here.
And because of this the time complexity is exponential complexity.
And here we see that it's very time consuming process.
Now to understand the problem let's look at the recursive tree of this algorithm here.
So if we calculate the Fibonacci for for the recursive tree is going to be like this.
So to calculate for we have to calculate three and two.
Then to calculate three we have to calculate two and one.
And it continues like now what is the problem over here.
The problem is we solve this subproblem multiple times.
So we are solving the Fibonacci two over here.
And we are solving the Fibonacci two over here.
So by saving the results we can eliminate one of these.
So let's say if I save the result in this case we don't need to calculate the Fibonacci two.
We are just going to take it from the memory.
And this is going to increase the efficiency of the algorithm.
So that's exactly what the dynamic programming is meant for.
So by saving the results of the recursive calls we can increase the efficiency of the algorithm.
So this is our algorithm that we have created before.
So let's convert this algorithm to the dynamic programming using the top down memoization.
So as I mentioned in this case we are just going to save it into the memory.
So to be able to do that first we need to pass as a parameter over here an object.
So I'm going to change the name and put it like this.
So before it was taking one parameter and now I'm passing over here another parameter which is going
to be memo as an object.
Then first we need to check that if this value exists in this object or not.
So we are going to write the if condition like this.
So we are checking that if this result is already calculated or not.
So if it is calculated we are just returning from here.
Otherwise we are going to use the recursive call to calculate it and save it into the memo object.
So in this case you see that here we are calculating it before we were returning.
Just this one now here calculating it and saving it into the memory and the return the value from the
memory by using this key.
So as you can see in three steps, we can easily convert the divide and conquer algorithm into the dynamic
programming algorithm.
Now, the last thing that I want to show you over here, let's see how this object is populated when
we run this code.
So here we have the Fibonacci code.
So initially the object is going to be like this.
So here let's say we are calculating it for Fibonacci six.
And initially we know that Fibonacci one and two is going to be zero and one.
The next step is we need to find the recursive value of f6.
So Fibonacci six.
We know that is calculated based on the Fibonacci four and five.
Now if you go to five, we see that five is empty, so we need to calculate it for five also.
So five will be calculated based on previous elements.
So three and four.
So if you go to four we see that it's empty.
So four will be calculated based on the previous result.
Then it continues like this until we reach F3.
So F3 is calculated based on F1 and F2.
And we know the values of f1 and f2 which is going to be zero plus one.
Then based on that we can calculate the F4 which is going to be one plus one, which is two.
Then we can calculate the F5 which is going to be one plus two is equal to three, then we can calculate
F6, which is going to be two plus three is going to be five.
So that's how the population of this object is going to look like when we are using the top down memorization
approach.
